title: Week 4 Worklog
content:
Week 4 Objectives: Review VPC networking and access control with Security Groups. Learn about EC2, Linux server access, and preparing a Node.js environment. Tasks to be carried out this week: Day Task Start Date Completion Date Reference Material 2 - Review VPCs and CIDR and identify address ranges for the VPC and its subnets.
- Distinguish public and private subnets using their routing configuration.
- Study local routes, routes to an Internet Gateway, and subnet route table associations.
- Compare Security Groups and Network ACLs: scope, inbound/outbound rules, and stateful versus stateless filtering.
- Review the VPC lab network configuration before preparing EC2. 26/10/2026 26/10/2026 Amazon VPC 4 - Check the VPC, public subnet, route table, and Internet Gateway for the office practice session.
- Learn the purposes of AMIs, instance types, EBS, and key pairs when launching EC2.
- Follow the guide to select Amazon Linux, configure storage, and name the instance.
- Select the subnet and configure a public IP and Security Group; study restricting SSH to the client IP.
- Try launching the instance, check its status, and record connection details. 28/10/2026 28/10/2026 Amazon EC2 5 - Read the SSH instructions covering the server address, ec2-user login, and private key file.
- Learn to check the IP address, port 22, and Security Group rules when a connection fails.
- Learn pwd, ls, cd, mkdir, cat, and nano for working with Linux directories and files.
- Read about installing Node.js with nvm and checking versions with node -v and npm -v.
- Study Git and the steps for transferring application source code to the server. 29/10/2026 29/10/2026 Connect to EC2 Linux 6 - At the office, continue checking EC2 connectivity and the Node.js, npm, and Git setup steps.
- Try creating a small Node.js application with an endpoint that returns a test response.
- Study the listening address, application port, and Security Group rules needed for client access.
- Try requests from the server and browser and compare responses with application logs.
- Record actual results and review lab instances, EBS storage, and network resources before cleanup. 30/10/2026 30/10/2026 Node.js on EC2 Week 4 Achievements: Expected to better understand connectivity from the internet to EC2 through subnets, route tables, and Security Groups. Expected to learn AMI selection, key pair creation, Linux instance launch, and SSH access. The practical goal is to run a simple Node.js application; deployment results will be updated based on actual practice.
